questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of length?
questions.explain: The metre (m) is the SI unit of length.

questions.prompt: Why are handspans not good units for measuring?
options: They are different for different people
questions.explain: Body parts vary in size from person to person, so results don't agree.

questions.prompt: A broken ruler is used. The pencil starts at the 2.0 cm mark and ends at the 16.5 cm mark. How long is the pencil?
questions.hint: Subtract the starting mark from the ending mark.

questions.prompt: To avoid parallax error, where should your eye be when reading a scale?
options: To the left of the mark
To the right of the mark
questions.explain: Looking straight down (perpendicular to the scale) avoids parallax error.

questions.prompt: Order these units from SMALLEST to LARGEST.
Put the steps in order to measure a curved line on a map.
steps: Lay a thread carefully along the curved line
Mark the thread where the line ends
Straighten the thread along a ruler
Read the length between the start and the mark
questions.explain: A thread turns a curve into a straight length you can measure.

questions.prompt: Match each measurement to the most suitable unit.
questions.explain: Choose a unit that gives a sensible-sized number.

questions.prompt: Explain why you should measure a length several times and take the average.
questions.modelAnswer: Every measurement can have small random errors, for example from placing the ruler slightly differently or reading the scale. Repeating the measurement and averaging reduces the effect of these errors, so the result is more reliable.
rubric: Averaging reduces the effect of errors
questions.explain: Repeating and averaging is a core scientific skill (IB Criterion B).
